problem: DRL controllers such as TD3 give reactive obstacle avoidance but lack object-location memory and language-level reasoning for long-horizon semantic indoor navigation; closed-cloud LLM pipelines and closed-vocabulary detectors are also limiting.
motivation: Semantic indoor navigation in cluttered, partially occluded scenes needs both robust low-level control and high-level understanding of objects and spatial context. Combining a locally deployed VLM for open-vocabulary recognition with a persistent semantic memory and a learned mapless controller is a lightweight route to language-conditioned goal reaching.
key_idea: Two-stage pipeline: a local VLM plus LiDAR/odometry explores and stores object categories with estimated world coordinates in a JSON semantic memory, then a language query retrieves target coordinates that are handed to a TD3 target-point navigation policy.
insight: Based on the abstract only: decoupling semantic grounding (VLM + coordinate memory) from low-level control (TD3 on point goals) lets a small, local VLM support flexible natural language queries. The abstract reports that the VLM-based recognizer gives more reliable grounding and coordinate estimation than YOLO-World v2.6 and Grounding DINO, especially for flexible language queries. No quantitative ablation details are available.
method: Stage 1 semantic exploration: the robot explores using odometry and 2D LiDAR to build a geometric map while a locally deployed VLM recognizes objects.
Object coordinate estimation: detected objects are assigned estimated world coordinates (VLM detection combined with sensor geometry).
Persistent semantic memory: object categories and coordinates are stored in a structured JSON file.
Stage 2 language grounding: a natural language query is matched against the JSON memory to retrieve target coordinates.
TD3 target-point policy: a DRL policy performs mapless navigation to the retrieved point using odometry and RealSense RGB-D perception.

Evaluation: ROS-integrated realistic simulation, compared with an Artificial Potential Field (APF) baseline using the same VLM and with DRL + GPT-4o mini; the recognition module is compared with YOLO-World v2.6 and Grounding DINO.

setting.backbone: Locally deployed VLM (unspecified in abstract, for recognition) + TD3 DRL policy (trained)
setting.training_data: TD3 trained in simulation (details not given in abstract); VLM used as-is
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands from TD3 toward a target point

results: The abstract claims consistent goal-reaching and improved navigation efficiency over an APF baseline using the same VLM and over a DRL + GPT-4o mini configuration. The VLM recognizer is also reported as more reliable than YOLO-World v2.6 and Grounding DINO for grounding and coordinate estimation. No numbers are given.
limitations: Evaluated only in ROS-integrated simulation with no real-robot results reported in the abstract
Requires a prior exploration stage to build the semantic memory (a static-scene assumption), and object coordinate estimation errors propagate to the controller
Full text and quantitative results are unavailable, so the claims are unverified
